job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

response.passage: Mr. Rao stood with his students, Arjun and Meera, before the crumbling lighthouse at Devgad. 'This structure was built in 1892 to guide ships away from the jagged rocks,' Mr. Rao explained, pointing at the rusted iron lantern room. Arjun touched the cold stone wall and asked, 'Did the lighthouse stop working because the ships stopped coming here?' Mr. Rao shook his head. 'No, Arjun. The lighthouse became obsolete because the government installed a modern GPS beacon on the nearby cliff in 1954. The light failed to guide ships effectively once the new technology arrived.' Meera looked at the tall tower and sighed, 'It looks so tired and lonely.' Mr. Rao smiled gently. 'It is not tired, Meera. It is simply a retired sentinel. The lighthouse remains standing because its thick granite base was designed to withstand the violent monsoon winds that batter this coast every year.' Arjun looked at the 45 steps leading to the top. 'If the base is strong, does that mean the lantern room is also strong?' Mr. Rao laughed, 'Not necessarily. The lantern room is made of thin iron, which rusts easily in the salty air.'
response.summary: Mr. Rao explains the history and structural purpose of the old Devgad lighthouse to his students. He clarifies why the lighthouse was replaced by modern technology and why its base remains sturdy despite its age.
